 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Jake Bauers is moving on.
 The first baseman is declining the qualifying offer from the Milwaukee Brewers and signing a four-year deal worth $58 million with the Boston Red Sox , according to ESPN's Jeff Passan.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bauers, the National League Championship Series MVP, had a career year for the Brewers in 2026. He became an integral piece to their World Series run, batting .266 with a .874 OPS and 26 home runs.
 Where to buy Brewers World Series front pages, T-shirts, hats, merch 
 His homer on an 11-pitch at-bat against Blake Snell in Game 3 of the NLCS to give the Brewers the lead was one of the most iconic moments from the championship run.
 Bauers had an offer for one year and $23 million on the table from Milwaukee, but the club wasn't willing to match that contract length for the 31-year-old first baseman.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement By Bauers signing elsewhere, the Brewers will receive a Competitive Balance A Round pick in the draft.
 Bauers, who first came to the Brewers in a minor trade for prospect Jace Avina prior to the 2024 season, called Milwaukee "home" earlier this week as he weighed his options.
 "I think you just got to sit down and really think about everything, right?" he said. "As much as all of it can be, it's about letting things come to you and taking it day by day. You really got to sit down and weigh the options, think about what you want the future to look like and move forward from there."
 The right choice for Bauers, in the end, was the guaranteed money. He will return to collect his ring with the Red Sox Sept. 14 at American Family Field, and that will not be the last time he comes back to Milwaukee to an ovation.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "We're gonna be coming back old and gray," Bauers said.
